issues.description: Storing raw credit card numbers (cardNumber) in plaintext violates PCI-DSS compliance. Payment card data should never be stored in application memory or transmitted to your server.
issues.suggestion: Use a payment gateway like Stripe, Square, or PayPal. Never handle raw card numbers in your application. Use tokenization where the payment provider handles sensitive card data and returns a token.

issues.description: Storing CVV (card verification value) is a severe PCI-DSS violation. CVV must never be stored after authorization, even temporarily.
issues.suggestion: Remove CVV from the PaymentDetails interface. Use a PCI-compliant payment gateway that handles CVV validation during the payment flow without your server ever receiving this data.

issues.description: Storing last four digits of card number in database without proper encryption or security controls. Even partial card data requires PCI compliance.
issues.suggestion: Let your payment gateway store all card-related data. Only store payment transaction IDs and status in your database. Reference the payment gateway for payment details.

issues.description: Console.error logging payment failures may expose sensitive payment information in logs, which is a security and compliance risk.
issues.suggestion: Use structured logging with sensitive data redaction. Log only non-sensitive identifiers (user ID, transaction ID) and error codes. Never log payment details or error messages containing card data.

issues.description: Card number validation only checks length === 16, but valid card numbers can be 13-19 digits (Amex is 15, Visa/MC are 16, etc.). This will reject valid cards.
issues.suggestion: Use the Luhn algorithm for card validation or rely on your payment gateway's validation. Support card lengths 13-19 digits if you must validate client-side.

issues.description: CVV validation accepts both 3 and 4 digits, but doesn't verify this matches the card type. American Express uses 4-digit CVV, others use 3 digits.
issues.suggestion: Remove CVV handling entirely and use a payment gateway. If client-side validation is needed, match CVV length to card type (detect via BIN/IIN range).

issues.description: Expiry date validation parses year as '2000 + parseInt(year)' which will break in 2100. Also, comparing dates without considering the day-of-month can cause false positives.
issues.suggestion: Parse as full 4-digit year or handle 2-digit years properly (20XX vs 21XX). Compare expiry at end-of-month: new Date(2000 + parseInt(year), parseInt(month), 0, 23, 59, 59)

issues.description: Date comparison 'expiryDateObj < new Date()' checks exact timestamp, but cards are valid through the last day of the expiry month, not the first day.
issues.suggestion: Set expiry date to the last moment of the expiry month before comparing: const lastDayOfMonth = new Date(2000 + parseInt(year), parseInt(month), 0, 23, 59, 59, 999);

issues.description: No validation that 'payment.amount' matches the calculated amount. A malicious client could send incorrect amount and bypass pricing.
issues.suggestion: Remove 'amount' from PaymentDetails interface. Always calculate amount server-side and never trust client-provided prices. Use: const amount = calculateSubscriptionPrice(tier);

issues.description: SQL query uses parameterized queries, which is good, but the 'db.query' implementation is imported and not validated. Ensure it properly escapes parameters.
issues.suggestion: Verify that the db.query function uses prepared statements. Consider using an ORM like TypeORM or Prisma for additional type safety and SQL injection protection.

issues.description: Raw SQL query with JSON.stringify for features array. While parameterized, this creates a PostgreSQL JSON column vulnerability if db.query doesn't handle types correctly.
issues.suggestion: Use database-native JSON types with proper ORM support. Validate that db.query properly handles JSON parameters. Consider using jsonb column type for better performance and querying.

issues.description: No error handling if database query fails. Function would throw unhandled exception.
issues.suggestion: Wrap database calls in try-catch blocks. Return null or throw a custom error with proper error message: try { const rows = await db.query(...); } catch (err) { throw new DatabaseError('Failed to check feature access'); }

issues.description: Accessing 'rows[0]' without checking array length could throw if implementation changes. Already checked, but defensive programming suggests using 'rows[0]?' or const subscription = rows[0];
issues.suggestion: Use optional chaining or explicit null checks: const subscription = rows[0]; if (!subscription) { return false; }

issues.description: JSON.parse without try-catch can throw if database contains malformed JSON. This would crash the function.
issues.suggestion: Add error handling: try { const features = JSON.parse(subscription.features); } catch { console.error('Malformed features JSON'); return false; }

issues.description: No transaction wrapping around payment charge and subscription upgrade. If upgradeUserSubscription fails, user is charged but not upgraded.
issues.suggestion: Wrap chargeCard and upgradeUserSubscription in a database transaction. On failure, rollback payment. Better yet, use idempotent payment tokens and verify webhook confirmation before upgrading.

issues.description: Magic numbers for pricing (9.99, 49.99) are hardcoded. Changes to pricing require code changes and redeployment.
issues.suggestion: Store pricing in database or configuration file. Use environment variables or a pricing service: const pricing = await getPricingFromConfig(); This allows dynamic pricing updates.

issues.description: Tax rate (8%) and processing fee (2.9%) are hardcoded constants. Tax rates vary by jurisdiction and should be configurable.
issues.suggestion: Calculate tax based on user location/billing address. Use a tax calculation service like Avalara or TaxJar. Store rates in configuration: const taxRate = await getTaxRate(billingAddress);

issues.description: Processing fee calculation (2.9%) appears to be a percentage, but typical payment processor fees are 2.9% + $0.30 flat fee. This undercalculates costs.
issues.suggestion: Use accurate fee structure: const fee = (basePrice * 0.029) + 0.30; Consider using payment gateway's fee calculation API.

issues.description: Feature lists are hardcoded. Adding new features requires code changes. Premium and Enterprise features are duplicated.
issues.suggestion: Store feature definitions in database or configuration: const features = await getFeaturesByTier(tier); Use feature flags service like LaunchDarkly for dynamic feature management.

issues.description: Function 'processPremiumPayment' returns boolean for success/failure, but throws errors for validation failures. Inconsistent error handling pattern.
issues.suggestion: Be consistent: either throw errors for all failures or return Result<Success, Error> type. Recommended: throw custom errors (PaymentValidationError, PaymentProcessingError) for all cases.

issues.description: Function 'validatePaymentDetails' is private but contains complex validation logic that should be unit tested. Cannot be tested in isolation.
issues.suggestion: Export validation functions for testing: export function validatePaymentDetails(...). Or better, remove card validation entirely and rely on payment gateway.

issues.description: chargeCard function performs synchronous string slicing operation before database call. Minor, but could be optimized.
issues.suggestion: Inline the operation: await db.query(query, [payment.cardNumber.slice(-4), amount, 'completed']); or use payment gateway tokens instead.

issues.description: hasFeatureAccess queries database every time a feature check is needed. High-frequency checks will cause N+1 query problem.
issues.suggestion: Cache subscription data in Redis or memory cache: const subscription = await getSubscriptionFromCache(userId); Invalidate cache on subscription updates. Set TTL to prevent stale data.

issues.description: getUserSubscription queries database without any caching. Multiple calls for same user will result in redundant queries.
issues.suggestion: Implement caching strategy: cache.get(`subscription:${userId}`) || await fetchAndCacheSubscription(userId). Use cache invalidation on subscription changes.

issues.description: No input validation for userId parameter across all functions. Empty strings or malformed IDs could cause issues.
issues.suggestion: Add input validation: if (!userId || typeof userId !== 'string') { throw new ValidationError('Invalid userId'); } Consider using UUID validation library.

issues.description: No logging for successful payment processing. Audit trails are essential for financial transactions.
issues.suggestion: Add structured logging: logger.info('Payment processed', { userId, tier, amount, transactionId }); Use logging service for compliance and debugging.

issues.description: Subscription validity is set to exactly 1 year from now. No handling for different billing cycles (monthly, annual).
issues.suggestion: Add billingCycle parameter: function upgradeUserSubscription(userId, tier, billingCycle: 'monthly' | 'annual'). Calculate validUntil based on cycle.

issues.description: No rate limiting on payment processing functions. Vulnerable to brute force attacks on payment endpoints.
issues.suggestion: Implement rate limiting: use express-rate-limit or similar. Limit payment attempts per user/IP. Add CAPTCHA for repeated failures.

codeQuality.summary: CRITICAL SECURITY ISSUES FOUND - This code has severe PCI-DSS compliance violations that make it illegal to deploy in production. The application handles raw credit card numbers and CVV data, which is a critical security and regulatory violation. Additionally, there are 5 critical security issues, 6 high-severity bugs/security concerns, 8 medium-severity issues, and several low/info items. Score: 25/100. IMMEDIATE ACTION REQUIRED: (1) Replace all payment handling with PCI-compliant payment gateway (Stripe/Square/PayPal), (2) Remove cardNumber and CVV from codebase, (3) Implement database transactions, (4) Add proper error handling and logging, (5) Fix pricing and tax calculation logic, (6) Add comprehensive test coverage for critical payment logic.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Main payment processing function handling real financial transactions. Bugs here could result in monetary loss, failed payments, or unauthorized access to premium features.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test successful payment flow for both premium and enterprise tiers. Test validation failure scenarios (invalid payment details, insufficient amount). Test payment gateway failure scenarios. Test that subscription upgrade occurs only after successful payment. Mock db.query and chargeCard to isolate logic.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Card validation is security-critical. Improper validation could allow invalid cards to be processed or reject valid cards.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test valid 16-digit card numbers. Test invalid lengths (15, 17 digits). Test CVV validation for 3 and 4 digits, reject 2 or 5+ digits. Test expiry format validation (MM/YY). Test expired cards are rejected (past month/year). Test edge case of current month expiry. Test non-numeric input handling.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Pricing calculation errors could lead to undercharging/overcharging customers, causing revenue loss or legal issues.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test premium tier returns 9.99 + (9.99 * 0.08) + (9.99 * 0.029) = 11.0891. Test enterprise tier returns 49.99 + (49.99 * 0.08) + (49.99 * 0.029) = 55.4391. Verify precision/rounding to 2 decimal places for currency.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Actual payment processing function. Failures here mean lost revenue or duplicate charges.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test successful charge creates payment record with correct last 4 digits, amount, and 'completed' status. Test database error handling returns false without throwing. Test card number slicing works for 16-digit numbers. Mock db.query to test both success and failure paths.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Controls access to paid features. Bugs could grant unauthorized access or fail to upgrade paying customers.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test premium tier grants correct features: ['unlimited_todos', 'priority_support', 'custom_themes']. Test enterprise tier grants all features including 'api_access' and 'team_collaboration'. Test validUntil is set to exactly 1 year from now. Test UPSERT logic handles both new subscriptions and upgrades. Mock db.query and verify query parameters.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Feature access control. Incorrect logic could allow free users to access premium features or block paying customers.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test returns false when user has no subscription. Test returns false when subscription is expired (validUntil < now). Test returns true when feature exists and subscription valid. Test returns false when feature not in user's tier. Test handles JSON parsing of features array correctly. Mock db.query to return various subscription states.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Retrieves subscription data used throughout the application. Incorrect data could cause widespread issues.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test returns null when user has no subscription. Test correctly maps database row to Subscription interface (userId, tier, validUntil as Date object, features as parsed array). Test handles all tier types (free, premium, enterprise). Mock db.query to return various subscription records.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Date comparison bugs are common and could incorrectly reject valid cards or accept expired ones.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test card expiring in current month and year (should be valid). Test card expired last month (should be invalid). Test year 2099 rollover handling. Test invalid date formats like '13/23', '00/22', '1/22' (single digit month).

untestedPaths.reasoning: Boundary condition that should be tested to ensure exact amount payments are accepted.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test payment.amount exactly equals calculated subscription price (should succeed). Test payment.amount is 0.01 less than required (should throw 'Insufficient payment amount'). Test payment.amount is greater than required (should succeed with overpayment).

untestedPaths.reasoning: String slicing could fail with unexpected input lengths.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test with exactly 16-digit card number. Test behavior if cardNumber is shorter than 4 characters (edge case that shouldn't occur due to validation, but worth defensive test). Verify last 4 digits are correctly extracted.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Error path that prevents invalid payments must be tested.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Pass payment with invalid card number (15 digits), verify Error('Invalid payment details') is thrown and no database operations occur.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Prevents undercharging, must be tested thoroughly.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Pass payment.amount = 5.00 for premium tier (requires ~11.09), verify Error('Insufficient payment amount') thrown and no charge occurs.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Must handle payment gateway failures gracefully without upgrading subscription.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Mock chargeCard to return false, verify processPremiumPayment returns false and upgradeUserSubscription is never called. Ensures no free upgrades on payment failure.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Each validation rule must be tested independently to ensure all invalid inputs are caught.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test each validation failure: cardNumber.length !== 16, cvv not 3 or 4 digits, invalid expiry format, expired card. Each should return false.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Different tiers must receive correct feature sets.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test premium tier receives only 3 basic features. Test enterprise tier receives all 5 features including team_collaboration and api_access. Verify feature arrays are exactly as expected.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Free users must not access premium features.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Mock db.query to return empty array (no subscription), verify hasFeatureAccess returns false for any feature.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Expired subscriptions must lose access immediately.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Mock db.query to return subscription with validUntil = yesterday, verify hasFeatureAccess returns false even if feature is in features array.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Must handle users without subscriptions.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Mock db.query to return empty array, verify getUserSubscription returns null (not undefined or throwing error).

untestedPaths.location: Database error handling in all async functions
untestedPaths.reasoning: Database failures should be handled gracefully without corrupting data or losing customer payments.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test each async function with mocked db.query throwing database errors. Verify processPremiumPayment doesn't lose payment data. Verify errors are logged appropriately. Test transaction rollback scenarios if implemented.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Date math can have edge cases around leap years and month boundaries.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test subscription created on Feb 29 (leap year) correctly expires on Feb 28/29 next year. Test Dec 31 subscription expires on Dec 31 next year. Verify setFullYear correctly handles year increment.

untestedPaths.location: Null/undefined input handling across all functions
untestedPaths.reasoning: Functions should handle invalid inputs gracefully.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test processPremiumPayment with null userId, undefined payment object. Test validatePaymentDetails with null/undefined fields. Test hasFeatureAccess with empty string userId. Verify appropriate errors thrown or false returned.

untestedPaths.location: SQL injection vectors in database queries
untestedPaths.reasoning: Even with parameterized queries, input validation prevents attack attempts.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test userId inputs like "'; DROP TABLE subscriptions; --" are safely handled by parameterized queries. Test special characters in features array. Verify all db.query calls use parameterized queries (code review test).

testCoverage.summary: CRITICAL RISK: This file has 0% test coverage despite containing payment processing, financial calculations, and subscription management logic. Found 7 untested functions with 0 tests written. Identified 22 critical untested paths including payment validation, pricing calculations, card charging, and subscription upgrades. Missing tests for error handling, edge cases (expired cards, insufficient payments, database failures), and security scenarios (SQL injection, invalid inputs). Immediate action required: This code should NOT be in production without comprehensive test coverage. Priority: Write tests for processPremiumPayment, validatePaymentDetails, and calculateSubscriptionPrice first as these directly handle money. Then cover hasFeatureAccess to prevent unauthorized feature access. Estimated 50+ test cases needed for adequate coverage.

suggestions.description: Extract magic numbers into named constants at module level
suggestions.benefits: Makes pricing configuration centralized and easier to update, improves testability by allowing constants to be mocked, enables reuse across multiple functions, makes business logic more transparent

suggestions.description: Extract expiry date validation into separate function
suggestions.benefits: Each validation rule becomes independently testable, improves code readability with descriptive function names, makes it easier to add new validation rules, enables reuse of validation logic in other contexts

suggestions.description: Extract feature mapping into a configuration object and create utility function
suggestions.benefits: Centralizes feature configuration making it easier to manage, eliminates conditional logic for feature selection, improves testability by making date calculation mockable, makes subscription duration configurable

suggestions.description: Extract SQL queries into constants for better maintainability and potential reuse
suggestions.benefits: Centralizes all SQL queries for easier maintenance and review, prevents SQL typos and inconsistencies, makes it easier to migrate to query builders or ORMs later, improves code organization

suggestions.description: Use guard clauses to reduce nesting and improve readability
suggestions.benefits: Reduces nesting from 2 levels to 0, improves readability with early returns, introduces descriptive variable for expiry check, follows guard clause pattern

suggestions.description: Extract subscription data transformation into a reusable mapper function
suggestions.benefits: Adds error handling for JSON parsing, centralizes data transformation logic, improves type safety with SubscriptionRow interface, makes code more maintainable and testable, eliminates code duplication

suggestions.description: Extract subscription expiry check into reusable utility function
suggestions.benefits: Creates reusable subscription validation logic, improves testability by isolating date comparison, makes intent clearer with descriptive function name, handles both Date and string inputs

suggestions.description: Add explicit payment status type and improve error handling with custom error classes
suggestions.benefits: Replaces boolean return with structured result type, enables better error handling with custom error classes, provides more detailed error messages, allows returning transaction details for auditing, improves API clarity

suggestions.description: Add type safety for sensitive payment data and improve security
suggestions.benefits: Adds compile-time safety for sensitive payment data, prevents accidental misuse of payment fields, centralizes validation through factory function, improves security by making sensitive data types explicit

suggestions.description: Use nullish coalescing and optional chaining for safer property access
suggestions.benefits: Adds null safety for edge cases where properties might be undefined, prevents runtime errors from accessing properties on null/undefined, follows modern TypeScript best practices

refactorings.summary: Found 10 high-impact refactoring opportunities in src/premium.ts. Key improvements: (1) Extract magic numbers and feature mappings into module-level constants for centralized configuration, (2) Split validation logic into separate, testable functions, (3) Extract SQL queries into named constants, (4) Create reusable data transformation and validation utilities, (5) Improve error handling with custom error classes and structured return types, (6) Add type safety for sensitive payment data. These refactorings will significantly improve testability (addressing the critical lack of tests mentioned in comments), maintainability, and security of the payment processing logic.

recommendations.description: IMMEDIATE: Remove all raw credit card and CVV handling code. This violates PCI-DSS compliance and is illegal to deploy. Integrate with a PCI-compliant payment gateway (Stripe, Square, or PayPal) that handles all sensitive card data through tokenization. Never store or process raw card numbers in your application.

Add comprehensive test coverage for payment processing logic (currently 0%). Start with processPremiumPayment, validatePaymentDetails, calculateSubscriptionPrice, and chargeCard. These functions handle financial transactions and must have 100% branch coverage to prevent revenue loss and payment failures. Minimum 50+ test cases needed.

Implement database transactions to wrap payment charge and subscription upgrade operations. Currently, if upgradeUserSubscription fails after chargeCard succeeds, customers are charged without receiving premium access. Use BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK or your ORM's transaction support.

Fix client-controlled pricing vulnerability: Remove 'amount' field from PaymentDetails interface. Always calculate subscription price server-side using calculateSubscriptionPrice() and never trust client-provided amounts. This prevents malicious users from setting arbitrary prices.

Extract all magic numbers and hardcoded business logic into configuration constants or database tables. Move pricing ($9.99, $49.99), tax rates (8%), processing fees (2.9%), and feature lists into centralized configuration. This enables pricing changes without code deployment and improves maintainability.
